# Sysadmin agent tools

The `sysadmin` agent (`sysadmin_agent`) publishes 11 tools to the [Tool Registry](../TOOL_REGISTRY.md). This page is generated from the agent's code: names, descriptions and parameters come from the tool definitions, action classes from `audit.ToolClassification`, and capabilities and eligibility from the agent card options. Capability names are defined in the [capability vocabulary](capabilities.md).

| Tool | Action class | Capabilities |
|---|---|---|
| [`check_disk`](#check_disk) | read | `host_disk` |
| [`check_host`](#check_host) | read | `process_status` |
| [`check_memory`](#check_memory) | read | `host_memory` |
| [`get_host_logs`](#get_host_logs) | read | `logs` |
| [`get_pgbackrest_status`](#get_pgbackrest_status) | read | `backup_status` |
| [`read_pg_log_file`](#read_pg_log_file) | read | `logs` |
| [`restart_container`](#restart_container) | destructive | `process_restart` |
| [`restart_service`](#restart_service) | destructive | `process_restart` |
| [`restore_from_backup`](#restore_from_backup) | destructive | `data_restore` |
| [`run_pgbackrest_backup`](#run_pgbackrest_backup) | write | `backup_run` |
| [`verify_restore_recovery`](#verify_restore_recovery) | read | `recovery_result` |

## `check_disk`

Show disk utilization on the host (df -h). Use to determine whether the database stopped due to a full data or log volume.

- **Action class:** read
- **Capabilities:** `host_disk`
- **Fleet eligible:** no
- **Auto-remediation eligible:** no
- **See also:**
  - [SYSADMIN_AGENT.md › `check_disk`](../SYSADMIN_AGENT.md#check_disk)

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `run_on_host` | boolean | no | If true, run df on the VM host OS instead of inside the container. Ignored for systemd targets. |
| `target` | string | no | Server ID from infrastructure config. When omitted, runs df on the agent host. |

## `check_host`

Check the status of the database process on the host. For Docker/Podman targets, inspects the container state. For systemd targets, shows the service ActiveState and SubState.

- **Action class:** read
- **Capabilities:** `process_status`
- **Fleet eligible:** no
- **Auto-remediation eligible:** no
- **Example prompts:** "Is the alloydb-omni container running?"
- **See also:**
  - [SYSADMIN_AGENT.md › `check_host`](../SYSADMIN_AGENT.md#check_host)

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `target` | string | yes | Server ID from infrastructure config (e.g. 'prod_db'), or a connection string / port (e.g. 'host=127.0.0.1 port=5432' or '5432') when the server ID is unknown — resolved by port matching. |

## `check_memory`

Show memory utilization on the host (free -h). Use to detect OOM conditions that may have caused the database process to be killed.

- **Action class:** read
- **Capabilities:** `host_memory`
- **Fleet eligible:** no
- **Auto-remediation eligible:** no
- **See also:**
  - [SYSADMIN_AGENT.md › `check_memory`](../SYSADMIN_AGENT.md#check_memory)

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `run_on_host` | boolean | no | If true, run free on the VM host OS instead of inside the container. Ignored for systemd targets. |
| `target` | string | no | Server ID from infrastructure config. When omitted, runs free on the agent host. |

## `get_host_logs`

Retrieve recent log lines from the database process. For Docker/Podman uses 'docker/podman logs'. For systemd uses journalctl. Use when the DB is down and read_pg_log is unavailable.

- **Action class:** read
- **Capabilities:** `logs`
- **Fleet eligible:** no
- **Auto-remediation eligible:** no
- **Example prompts:** "Show the last 200 log lines from the prod_db container"
- **See also:**
  - [SYSADMIN_AGENT.md › `get_host_logs`](../SYSADMIN_AGENT.md#get_host_logs)

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `target` | string | yes | Server ID from infrastructure config, or a connection string / port — resolved by port matching. |
| `filter` | string | no | Optional substring to filter log lines (case-sensitive). |
| `lines` | integer | no | Number of recent log lines to return (default 100). |

## `get_pgbackrest_status`

Check pgBackRest backup-job health: stanza status, the most recent backup's label/time/type, whether it's stale relative to the expected schedule, and wal_continuity — whether the archived WAL needed to restore that backup to the end of the archive is present and unbroken (status continuous, broken, unverified or no_backup; broken lists the gaps and where recovery would stop). This is the backup-taking precondition — distinct from the database agent's get_backup_status, which checks WAL archiving health via pg_stat_archiver.

- **Action class:** read
- **Capabilities:** `backup_status`
- **Fleet eligible:** no
- **Auto-remediation eligible:** no
- **Example prompts:** "Check whether pgBackRest's last backup for prod_db is stale"
- **See also:**
  - [MUTATION_TOOLS.md › 1.13 `get_pgbackrest_status` — read-only inspector](../MUTATION_TOOLS.md#113-get_pgbackrest_status--read-only-inspector)
  - [SYSADMIN_AGENT.md › `get_pgbackrest_status`](../SYSADMIN_AGENT.md#get_pgbackrest_status)
  - [BACKUP.md › 2. pgBackRest job-level backup health](../BACKUP.md#2-pgbackrest-job-level-backup-health)

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `max_age_hours` | integer | no | How many hours old the most recent successful backup may be before it's considered stale. Default 25 (one day plus margin) — override to match the target's actual backup schedule. Zero or negative values fall back to the default; there is no way to force an immediate backup to read as stale via this parameter. |
| `stanza` | string | no | pgBackRest stanza name. When omitted, the only stanza present is used — an error if more than one exists. |
| `target` | string | no | Server ID from infrastructure config. Required whenever infrastructure config is loaded — omitting it then is treated as a resolution failure and errors loudly, not a request to run locally. Only leave this empty when no infrastructure config exists at all (a genuinely colocated deployment). If your connection_string/server ID doesn't match a known infrastructure entry, do not guess or omit target — report that as its own finding and escalate. |

## `read_pg_log_file`

Read the PostgreSQL log file directly from inside the container or pod (via exec). Works when Postgres is down — does not require a live database connection. Use get_host_logs for process stdout/stderr; use this tool for the PostgreSQL log file written by logging_collector.

- **Action class:** read
- **Capabilities:** `logs`
- **Fleet eligible:** no
- **Auto-remediation eligible:** no
- **See also:**
  - [SYSADMIN_AGENT.md › `read_pg_log_file`](../SYSADMIN_AGENT.md#read_pg_log_file)

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `target` | string | yes | Server ID from infrastructure config. |
| `filter` | string | no | Only return lines containing this string (case-insensitive). Useful for: ERROR, FATAL, PANIC, OOM, 'no space'. |
| `lines` | integer | no | Number of recent log lines to return (default 100). |
| `log_path` | string | no | Override the log directory path inside the container. Default: /var/lib/postgresql/data/log. |

## `restart_container`

Restart a Docker or Podman container hosting the database. Requires the server to have a container_runtime and container_name configured in infrastructure.json. Use restart_service for systemd-managed databases.

## `restore_from_backup`

Restore the database from the latest pgBackRest backup, overwriting the current data directory (destructive — requires operator approval). Restore-to-latest only: no point-in-time target. Refuses outright if the server is still accepting connections (pg_isready), or if the latest backup's WAL chain is not confirmed continuous to the end of the archive (wal_continuity.status other than continuous). Use only when get_pgbackrest_status confirms a healthy, non-stale backup with wal_continuity.status=continuous exists and the instance is confirmed down — never against a broken repo/stanza, a broken or unverified WAL chain, or a live instance. It keeps the WAL that was in pg_wal: moved aside before the restore, put back for recovery to replay past the end of the archive, and the segments past it pushed to the archive (pg_wal_tail: saved_to, replay_through_wal, pushed_to_archive); commits that were on disk but never archived are recovered rather than lost. On success it records where recovery should end (prediction: the archive end, any pg_wal tail, and the new timeline); after restarting the instance, call verify_restore_recovery to confirm where recovery actually ended.

- **Action class:** destructive
- **Capabilities:** `data_restore`
- **Fleet eligible:** no
- **Auto-remediation eligible:** no
- **See also:**
  - [MUTATION_TOOLS.md › 1.15 `restore_from_backup` — restore from latest pgBackRest backup](../MUTATION_TOOLS.md#115-restore_from_backup--restore-from-latest-pgbackrest-backup)
  - [BACKUP.md › 3. Restore from backup after data loss](../BACKUP.md#3-restore-from-backup-after-data-loss)

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `stanza` | string | no | pgBackRest stanza name. When omitted, the only stanza present is used — an error if more than one exists. |
| `target` | string | no | Server ID from infrastructure config. Required whenever infrastructure config is loaded — omitting it then is treated as a resolution failure and errors loudly, not a request to run locally. Only leave this empty when no infrastructure config exists at all (a genuinely colocated deployment). If your connection_string/server ID doesn't match a known infrastructure entry, do not guess or omit target — report that as its own finding and escalate. |

## `run_pgbackrest_backup`

Take a fresh pgBackRest backup (default type=full). Requires operator approval (Write action). Use only to remediate a STALE backup on an otherwise-healthy repo (get_pgbackrest_status status_code=0, backup_stale=true) — never against a broken repo/stanza (status_code != 0), which needs human investigation, not a new backup attempt.

- **Action class:** write
- **Capabilities:** `backup_run`
- **Fleet eligible:** no
- **Auto-remediation eligible:** no
- **See also:**
  - [MUTATION_TOOLS.md › 1.14 `run_pgbackrest_backup` — manual backup](../MUTATION_TOOLS.md#114-run_pgbackrest_backup--manual-backup)
  - [SYSADMIN_AGENT.md › `run_pgbackrest_backup`](../SYSADMIN_AGENT.md#run_pgbackrest_backup)
  - [BACKUP.md › 2. pgBackRest job-level backup health](../BACKUP.md#2-pgbackrest-job-level-backup-health)

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `stanza` | string | no | pgBackRest stanza name. When omitted, the only stanza present is used — an error if more than one exists. |
| `target` | string | no | Server ID from infrastructure config. Required whenever infrastructure config is loaded — omitting it then is treated as a resolution failure and errors loudly, not a request to run locally. Only leave this empty when no infrastructure config exists at all (a genuinely colocated deployment). If your connection_string/server ID doesn't match a known infrastructure entry, do not guess or omit target — report that as its own finding and escalate. |
| `type` | string | no | Backup type: full, diff, or incr. Default full — always valid regardless of backup history, unlike diff/incr which require a prior full backup to reference. |

## `verify_restore_recovery`

After restore_from_backup and the restart, check where PostgreSQL's recovery actually ended against where restore_from_backup predicted it would (the last WAL segment restored from the archive, and the new timeline). Reads PostgreSQL's own recovery log lines. status: verified (as predicted), mismatch (stopped early, went past, or a different timeline — report it), not_found (no completed recovery in the log yet: the instance may not be restarted, or recovery failed before promotion), unverified (no prediction recorded for this target, or nothing restored from the archive). Also returns the exact LSN redo ended at, and replayed_through_wal when recovery replayed WAL that restore_from_backup put back into pg_wal past the archive. Read-only.

- **Action class:** read
- **Capabilities:** `recovery_result`
- **Fleet eligible:** no
- **Auto-remediation eligible:** no

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `target` | string | yes | Server ID from infrastructure config — the same target restore_from_backup was called with. |
